domain: Digital Commons Governance / Knowledge Infrastructure / Platform Constitutionalism
topic_summary: Analysis of Wikipedia's notability guidelines (WP:N) as a contested kernel where the same codified text is read by deletionists as a necessary epistemic quality filter (coordination mechanism) versus inclusionists as a structural gatekeeping apparatus that systematically excludes marginalized knowledge. The disagreement is not about whether WP:N exists but what constraint it instantiates.

key_entities: Wikipedia Notability Guidelines (WP:N) - codified practice-norm governing article inclusion
Deletionist faction - editors emphasizing strict application of notability standards
Inclusionist faction - editors advocating broader inclusion criteria
Articles for Deletion process (AfD) - enforcement mechanism for notability disputes
Reliable Sources requirement - operational criterion defining notability threshold
Wikimedia Foundation - platform authority disclaiming interpretive control
key_tensions: Epistemic quality vs epistemic coverage (encyclopedia purity vs knowledge pluralism)
Formal neutrality vs structural bias (guideline claims universality while systematically favoring Western/institutional sources)
mechanisms: AfD deletion process - peer review mechanism for notability enforcement
Reliable Sources doctrine - citation hierarchy privileging institutional publishers
Admin discretion layer - unelected editors with deletion authority interpreting guidelines
absences: No mechanism for measuring what knowledge is lost through deletion (victim set invisible)
No audit of systemic bias in 'reliable source' availability across cultural/economic contexts
No revision mechanism for guidelines despite documented coverage gaps (women, Global South, non-Western knowledge systems)

axes.selection_reason: Core reading of kernel; rope hypothesis with coordination framing; establishes baseline constraint structure

axes.structural_delta: WP:N instantiates an extractive gatekeeping mechanism systematically excluding marginalized knowledge through culturally-biased reliable source requirements
axes.primary_observable: Demographic coverage gaps; deletion patterns by article subject identity; reliable source availability across cultural contexts
axes.selection_reason: Competing reading with structurally different constraint (different victim set, higher epsilon); snare hypothesis captures extractive framing

axes.structural_delta: WP:N instantiates a deliberative scaffold where notability is perpetually contested through AfD process, enabling evolutionary boundary negotiation
axes.primary_observable: AfD discussion length/complexity; guideline interpretation variance; revision frequency of edge cases
axes.selection_reason: Third structural position: neither quality filter nor gatekeeping but perpetual negotiation process; captures meta-level constraint on how disputes resolve

omegas.description: WMF disclaims interpretive authority over guidelines ('community decides') yet retains ultimate platform control. Is this authority structure functioning drift absorption (community can revise) or absent drift (WMF prevents structural revision)? Authority legitimacy ambiguous.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) - no formal mechanism for guideline revision despite documented coverage gaps

omegas.description: Is 'reliable sources' requirement a Mountain (epistemic necessity for verifiability) or Piton (policy choice that froze one verification method as universal)? If Mountain, inclusionist reading collapses to complaint about physics. If Piton, deletionist reading defends a chosen norm as necessary truth.
omegas.source: F03 (Hasty Generalization) - classification instability between readings depends on underlying status of verification requirement

omegas.description: No mechanism exists to measure what knowledge is lost through deletion. Victim set in inclusionist/institutional_capture readings is structurally invisible. Without measurement, cannot adjudicate between 'preventing spam' and 'systematic erasure' claims.
omegas.source: Extraction absence + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: Unelected admin authority interprets guidelines in deletion decisions. Is this a functional governance scaffold or concealed tangled_rope where admin class benefits from interpretive monopoly? Deletion authority concentration may warrant separate axis.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) - analysis operates within editor/reader frame; admin power structure treated as background

omegas.description: Documented coverage gaps for Global South, women, non-Western knowledge systems. Is this outcome of neutral guidelines applied to biased source availability (Mountain of information asymmetry) or outcome of guidelines designed to favor Western institutional sources (Snare)? Empirical question with classification implications.

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: 'reliable sources' requirement classification as Mountain vs Piton determines whether inclusionist reading is valid critique or category error. Generated omega_reliable_source_mountain to bound uncertainty. No F34: domain is platform governance / knowledge infrastructure, within model training scope. No F14: kernel decomposition deliberately generates competing readings from same lens.

readings.commitment: WP:N as necessary epistemic quality filter preventing commons degradation
readings.expected_structural_delta: Constraint is coordination Rope; beneficiary is readership (quality preservation); no victim set (spam/vanity excluded justly)

readings.commitment: WP:N as structural gatekeeping apparatus systematically excluding marginalized knowledge
readings.expected_structural_delta: Constraint is extractive Snare; beneficiary is institutional knowledge producers; victim is marginalized communities whose knowledge lacks 'reliable sources'

readings.expected_structural_delta: Constraint is governance Scaffold; notability is output of process not input; boundary negotiation is the mechanism

axiom_contradictions.basis: Deletionist axiom: epistemic quality requires exclusion of non-verified content (inclusion degrades commons). Inclusionist axiom: systematic exclusion based on culturally-biased verification standards is epistemic injustice (exclusion degrades commons). No single framework can hold both 'exclusion preserves quality' and 'exclusion constitutes injustice' as simultaneously true for the same knowledge.
